name: SEDM

paper.title: SEDM: Scalable Self-Evolving Distributed Memory for Agents

construction.unit: memory item: one short injectable snippet extracted from a task run, with a utility weight and provenance
construction.kept_as: extracted snippet (decisive reasoning or corrective step), deduplicated and canonicalized
construction.processing: package the run as an SCEC; extract one candidate; A/B replay with and without it; admit if S = ΔR − λL·ΔL − λT·ΔT ≥ η
construction.writer: not stated (extraction model and prompt are not described)

organization.structure: flat pool of weighted items, each paired with an abstracted general form; trajectory, query and insight graphs keep provenance
organization.stores: one repository of specific and general items

management.operations: weight update w ← w + α·Ū − β·f_use; promote stable items; merge near-duplicates; abstract recurring items into insights
management.conflicts: items whose injections repeatedly lower reward, or that contradict other rules, are demoted and removed below a threshold
management.forgetting: decay of rarely used or unhelpful items; removal or soft-delete below a weight threshold

retrieval.candidates: dense similarity over specific and general items
retrieval.selection: rank by s(q,m) = sim(q,m) × w(m); no reranker
retrieval.budget: same memory budget as baselines (size not stated); top-k not stated

use.context: selected items injected into the agent prompt
use.reasoning: the agent's own task loop (ReAct-style Search/Finish trace in the SCEC example)

classify.note: Admission and weights come from measured task feedback, but at read time the rule is fixed: similarity times weight. Merging and abstraction make management 'consolidate' rather than 'update in place'.

stages.ingestion: Each task run is packaged as a Self-Contained Execution Context (SCEC): inputs, outputs, summarised tool calls, seeds and config hashes, so it can be replayed without the original environment.
stages.construction: One candidate snippet is extracted per SCEC and tested by paired A/B replay (prompt with and without it); it is admitted only if the reward gain minus latency and token costs clears a threshold, and that score becomes its initial weight.
stages.organization: Admitted items sit in one weighted pool; right after admission each gets a general form with entities replaced by typed placeholders and a scaled-down weight.
stages.update: Weights move with realised utility and usage frequency; near-duplicates are merged, stable items promoted and abstracted, and items that keep hurting reward are demoted or removed.
stages.retrieval: Items are scored by embedding similarity to the query multiplied by their weight; specific and general forms compete in the same ranking, with no reranker.
stages.answer: Selected items are injected into the agent's prompt.
stages.learning: No model is trained; only per-item scalar weights change from observed outcomes.

summary: Memory items enter only after an A/B replay shows they raise reward net of latency and token cost; that measured gain becomes a weight that multiplies similarity at retrieval and keeps being updated, merged and abstracted for cross-task transfer.
notes: Paper v3 (2025-09-26) read from the arXiv PDF. No code: the abstract says code will be released on acceptance, and no official repository was found. Hyper-parameters λL, λT, η, α, β, top-k and the memory budget are not given. How SCEC replay and extraction are applied to LoCoMo dialogues is not described. The LoCoMo Table 1 rows for LoCoMo, ReadAgent, MemoryBank, MemGPT and A-Mem equal A-Mem's (2502.12110) GPT-4o-mini Table 1 values rounded to one decimal, under different category labels; see results notes.

sources.code_note: No official code: the paper says code will be released upon acceptance, and a GitHub search found no repository. Everything here follows the paper text, Eqs. 1-10 and Figure 2.

headline: A memory item is admitted only if replaying the same run with it beats replaying without it, net of latency and token cost; the net score is its starting weight.
Retrieval is plain similarity times that weight: no reranker and no LLM at read time.
The paper gives no values for the thresholds, trade-off weights, top-k or memory budget, and does not say how the replay test is run on LoCoMo dialogues.

fields.name: inputs, trace, output, tool summaries, seeds, config hashes
fields.what: everything needed to replay the run without the environment (Figure 2 shows thought/action/observation steps, the final answer, correctness, latency and token use)

write.how: wrap a finished run into an SCEC with summarised tool calls so it can be replayed anywhere
pull one candidate snippet from the SCEC; deduplicate, canonicalize, attach provenance
run the SCEC with the original prompt (A) and with the snippet injected (B); measure ΔR, ΔL, ΔT; may average several runs; jobs spread over workers
accept if S ≥ η; initial weight w₀ = max(0, S); otherwise discard
make a general form with typed placeholders; weight α·w (α < 1); generated alongside the A/B test
update weights from realised utility and usage; merge similar items without conflicts; demote or remove items that keep lowering reward

HotpotQA EM: no memory / G-Memory / SEDM

open_questions: How is an A/B replay with a task reward run on LoCoMo dialogue QA, and what is extracted from a conversation? The paper describes the pipeline only for agent task runs.
Gains over G-Memory on FEVER and HotpotQA (4 and 1 points) come without the number of test items, variance or the size of the shared memory budget.
The ablation adds the admission gate and the scheduler together with their weights; there is no run of weighting without the gate, or the gate without weighted retrieval.

glance.a: A short snippet taken from one task run (a decisive or corrective step), stored with a utility weight, provenance and a generalised copy.

glance.q: What decides whether it is stored?
glance.a: A paired replay of the same run with and without the snippet; it is kept only if the reward gain minus latency and token costs reaches a threshold.
Embedding similarity to the query times the item's weight; no reranker and no LLM step.

glance.q: Does memory change after it is written?
glance.a: Yes: weights follow observed utility and usage, similar items are merged, and harmful ones are demoted or removed.

glance.q: What does the answer model read?
glance.a: Its task prompt plus the selected items; the exact template and count are not given.

key_numbers.value: S = ΔR − λL·ΔL − λT·ΔT; keep if S ≥ η (values not given)

key_numbers.label: Initial weight
key_numbers.value: max(0, S); general form α·w, α < 1

discussion.takeaway: Gate memory writes with a replay test that measures whether an item actually helps, and reuse that measured gain as a weight at retrieval. On FEVER and HotpotQA this beats G-Memory with fewer tokens, but beats no memory at a token cost.

claims.claim: SEDM improves accuracy while using fewer tokens than a strong memory baseline.
claims.evidence: FEVER 66 vs 62 (G-Memory) with 2.47M vs 3.62M prompt tokens; HotpotQA 39 vs 38 with 3.88M vs 4.63M. Table 2, §4.3

claims.claim: Both the admission gate and the scheduler contribute.
claims.evidence: HotpotQA 34 → 37 → 39, FEVER 57 → 64 → 66 as SCEC then self-scheduling are added. Table 3, §4.4

claims.claim: Best on LoCoMo temporal and open-domain questions.
claims.evidence: Temporal F1 47.5 vs 32.4 for G-Memory. Table 1, §4.2 (open-domain: see reading)

claims.claim: Memory learned on one task transfers to another.
claims.evidence: FEVER-collected memory gives 41 on HotpotQA vs 39 in-domain; HotpotQA memory gives 64 on FEVER. Table 4, §4.5

limits: The paper has no limitations section.
It notes that dialogue memory from LoCoMo transfers poorly to the other two tasks (HotpotQA 34, the no-memory level).
reading: The text says SEDM has the best open-domain F1 and BLEU-1 on LoCoMo, but Table 1 shows G-Memory higher (53.5 vs 51.7 F1, 44.0 vs 37.0 BLEU-1); SEDM is best only on temporal.

The LoCoMo, ReadAgent, MemoryBank, MemGPT and A-Mem rows equal A-Mem's GPT-4o-mini Table 1 rounded to one decimal, but under different category names, and the paper does not say they were copied. §4.1 lists four question types while the table has five, including adversarial.
SEDM's LoCoMo run has no ablation, token count, embedder or description of how the replay reward is defined for dialogue QA.

The scheduler raises token use relative to the gate alone (FEVER 2.19M → 2.47M, HotpotQA 3.52M → 3.88M); the saving is only relative to G-Memory, and both memory methods use more tokens than no memory.
Every trade-off parameter (λL, λT, η, α, β), top-k and the shared memory budget are unreported, and there is no code, so the results cannot be reproduced from the paper.
α names both the utility step in Eq. 7 and the general-form weight scale in §3.4.

abstract.text: SEDM targets memory for long-running (multi-)agent systems, where stored trajectories pile up noise and cost. Each task run is packed into a self-contained, replayable context; a candidate memory item is kept only if replaying the run with it beats replaying without it, after charging for extra latency and tokens. The measured gain becomes a weight that multiplies embedding similarity at retrieval and keeps being revised, merged and generalised into placeholder forms that can move across tasks. On FEVER and HotpotQA with GPT-4o-mini it scores above G-Memory with fewer tokens, and it reports competitive LoCoMo scores and cross-task transfer.
